topics.label: Formation of PDEs
topics.summary: Forming a PDE by eliminating arbitrary constants or arbitrary functions, why a PDE has an arbitrary function in its general solution, and the Jacobian form Pp+Qq=R.

subtopics.label: General case: φ(u,v)=0
subtopics.summary: Eliminating φ gives a Lagrange equation whose coefficients are Jacobians.

topics.label: Equations of the Form F(p, q) = 0
topics.summary: Plane solutions z = ax + by + c with F(a,b)=0 give the complete integral; envelopes give the general integral.

topics.label: Equations of the Form F(z, p, q) = 0
topics.summary: Substituting u = x + ay reduces the PDE to an ODE in z and u.

topics.label: Equations of the Form F(x, p) = G(y, q)
topics.summary: Set both sides equal to a constant a, solve for p and q, then integrate dz = p dx + q dy.

topics.label: Clairaut's Form and the Singular Solution
topics.summary: Clairaut's complete integral by replacing p, q with constants, and the singular solution as the envelope of the family of planes.

topics.label: Lagrange's Linear Equation Pp + Qq = R
topics.summary: Characteristic curves, the auxiliary equations dx/P = dy/Q = dz/R, and the general solution φ(u,v)=0.

subtopics.label: Solving the auxiliary equations
subtopics.summary: Grouping and the method of multipliers.

topics.label: Linear First-Order PDEs by Separation of Variables
topics.summary: Product solutions with a separation constant, fixed by the given condition, and superposition for sums of exponentials.
